thesis: Natural Resource Partners L.P. is a Houston-based master limited partnership that owns mineral interests and other subsurface rights across the United States and collects royalties, overriding royalties, and lease fees from third-party operators. **[Fact]** The partnership does not mine, drill, or produce minerals; it leases acreage and receives cash from lessees (`NRP/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260227_rpt20251231_acc0001437749_26_006147.htm`, Business). **[Fact]** As of May 6, 2026, **13,250,412** common units were outstanding (`NRP/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260506_rpt20260331_acc0001437749_26_015150.htm`). **[Fact]** The partnership reports two operating segments: **Mineral Rights** (~**99%** of FY2025 revenues) and **Soda Ash** (a **49%** non-controlling equity interest in Sisecam Wyoming) (`same 10-K`). **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenues and other income were **$207.3 million**, down from **$268.0 million** in 2024 and **$370.0 million** in 2023 (`same 10-K`).
why_market_wrong: Yield-focused investors may treat NRP as a simple coal royalty bond and miss the breadth of the **~13 million acre** mineral footprint, including oil and gas, aggregates, and emerging carbon-sequestration and renewable lease opportunities. **[Inference]** K-1 partnership tax reporting and MLP structure can exclude the name from dividend screeners despite meaningful asset backing. **[Inference]** The market may be pricing Sisecam Wyoming's soda ash weakness as permanent, while the partnership's **$276 million** equity-method carrying value and Q1 2026 capital contribution suggest management still sees long-term option value (`10-Q_20260506`). **[Inference]** Post-2023 debt refinancing and distribution cuts to **$0.75** per quarter may look like peak-cycle normalization rather than a trough with bounded downside given **$30 million** cash and a **~0.4x** leverage ratio at March 31, 2026 (`10-Q_20260506` debt footnote).
